items.item: adversarial reviewer says escalate: The eval-case drop rule as specified cannot be implemented correctly by the design it prescribes. spec.md's Requirements and Acceptance say a case is dropped 'when nothing is left under its folder at HEAD', but spec.md's Design (and plan.md step 2) say the drop rule is 'one small pure function taking the parsed [--name-status -M diff] records ... so it is unit-testable without git'. A --name-status diff lists only files that changed between the merge base and HEAD; a file under the case folder that was never touched by the diff does not appear in those records at all, so the pure function has no way to know whether it still exists at HEAD. The consequence is concrete, not hypothetical: deleting one file out of a multi-file eval case (leaving the rest intact) would show a D under that case's path with no corresponding survivor visible to the function, and a diff-records-only implementation would have to either (a) wrongly flag the whole case as dropped (false positive park on a change that did not drop the case) or (b) under-detect real drops spread across several commits. The only way to honor the literal requirement is to also consult the tree at HEAD (e.g. git ls-tree -r --name-only HEAD <folder>), which plan.md's file list for plugin/gate/diff.py does not include and which the Design explicitly says the function avoids ('without git').; This exact gap was identified by the devil's advocate on this same phase-b panel (evidence/panel/b-1-advocate.md, point 3: '--name-status records list only changed paths, so they cannot tell whether an untouched file survives under the case folder... the nearest tool at hand is the filesystem... intent.md's own Constraints and OPERATING_MODEL §3 forbid the gate to judge [the working tree]'), but the conciliator's decision (evidence/panel/b-1-conciliator.json, evidence/decisions-b.json) closes only the narrower 'framework/ is out of scope' half of the flagged concern and explicitly declines to resolve this one ('they park for the owner as their own finding rather than being folded into this concern's closure'). No such finding is actually written into spec.md's Flagged concerns, plan.md's Risks, or any Open question in this diff -- it exists only as panel-member prose, so nothing in the committed design artifacts currently tells the owner, or the build session that will read plan.md at (c), that this gap exists or how to close it.; The planned tests cannot catch this: plan.md's Order of work (step 2) builds the drop-rule's own unit tests from 'the parser from step 1 as a fixture input, not live git', i.e. synthetic parsed-record fixtures rather than a real repository at two commits. The advocate makes the same point about the one eval-case acceptance test named in plan.md's Proof ('test_ratchets_drop_eval_case_folder_emptied_fails passes either way: in a clean fixture Path.exists() and git ls-tree HEAD agree'). Acceptance as written does not include a case that distinguishes 'folder empty at HEAD' from 'some file under the folder was deleted but others remain', so an implementation with this bug would ship green.
